Repo: /workspace/SuperGrok1.5, branch claude/h100-audit-maximal. H100 sm_90. SOLE builder (edit-war over). Current: 28/33 L3-TC (verified via wiring_check).

TASK: convert **SuperGrok2 (supergrok2) to L3-TC wgmma** on DECODER and VIT (mamba dormant). Target 28 -> 30/33.

**FOLLOW THE SPEC at `/workspace/.sg2_spec.md`** — read it fully; it's the builder-ready plan with file:line. Summary:
- The full SG2 meta-net (`sg2_meta_stages` in opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh) is ALREADY BUILT + fp64-parity-green — REUSE it, don't rebuild the math.
- 4 deliverables: (1) the in-kernel SEGMENTED SORT (the only big new device code — use index-tie-break **strategy A**, keep the oracle's perm builder in lock-step; tie-semantics is the #1 risk), (2) COMPOSE the meta-net into the decoder/vit megakernel as the optimizer phase (reuse the existing P2.4 SAM 2nd-pass for `st.sharpness`), (3) wire `st.sharpness` into the meta-net (`sharp_base`), (4) routing (wgmma_tail_opt_id supergrok2->10; launcher cases bind the FULL SG2 state [m|v|mu|slow|gru_state|sharpness|perm|unsort|meta-bundle|per-tensor-scalars] + bump min_state; dispatch.py cell sets + do_sam cadence). Per-tensor scalars DON'T fit the global FusedScalars — thread buffers via state/workspace.
- MAMBA: land dormant (code-present, gated OUT of _L3_WGMMA_CELLS). SG2's SAM double-forward + segmented sort may re-trip the mamba forward race (the recent fix covered prodigy/looksam, not SG2's path). VERIFY A/A/A on decoder/vit (expected clean via strategy A); keep mamba dormant unless A/A/A confirms clean.
- HONEST CAVEAT (carry it): SG2 reaches L3-TC + single-step parity but WON'T GROK — the CSA lightning-indexer fidelity gap (kernel drops idx_UQ, /sqrt(rank) vs /sqrt(d), diverges for N>64). Land it parity-clean; the gate includes an N>64 CSA fidelity PROBE that REPORTS the divergence (NOT a regression). Do NOT fake/suppress to force grok.

RULES: no suppression; parity vs `ops.supergrok2_batched_step` (single-step <1e-5; 200-step trajectory <1e-5) + fp64 (~3e-5, fp32 storage); A/A/A bit-determinism (segmented sort deterministic via strategy A); single-source math (supergrok2.h canonical; adjoint oracle supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h).
BUILD: `python setup.py build_ext --inplace` (sccache wired via the nvcc shim; TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR=/workspace/.torch_ext is exec-able). Export `TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR=/workspace/.torch_ext TMPDIR=/dev/shm/tmp`.
GATES (CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent): tail-gate (existing 28 stay green + SG2 decoder/vit PASS + A/A/A; implement the SG2 part-B gate per the spec, register the cells); wiring_check --require-all (SG2 decoder/vit -> PASS L3-TC; count 28 -> 30).
COMMIT locally if green (raw evidence in the message; end: Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>).
RETURN: raw gate output (SG2 dec/vit PASS + A/A/A result + the per-op parity numbers + the N>64 CSA fidelity probe), new count (expect 30/33), diff summary, build wall-time, and the honest grok caveat. If the sort tie-semantics or occupancy/smem resists, report it (land what passes; document the rest).

1	# SG2 -> L3-TC — builder spec (task #11). Decoder primary; vit delta; mamba DORMANT.
2	Last/hardest cell. The full SG2 meta-net is ALREADY BUILT (reuse, don't rebuild): sg2_meta_stages<Dims> (S0..S5 CSA/HCA/GRU/PEER/apply) in csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh, bound as sg2_meta_optimizer_tail (bindings.cpp:3599). Part-A fp64 parity GREEN (~1e-16, test_sg2_megakernel.py:96-135). OptId::SuperGrok2=10 exists (opt_components.cuh:56); current apply_optimizer<SuperGrok2> is just an Adam tail on st.smart_grad — NOT the meta-net.
3	
4	## 4 deliverables
5	1. In-kernel SEGMENTED SORT (STAGE -1, the only big new device code): per-tensor in-CTA bitonic sort of [N] |grad| keys ascending; write perm/unsort before S0. TIE TRAP: torch.sort on CUDA is UNSTABLE — reproduce THAT order, NOT argsort(stable). RECOMMENDED strategy A: tie-break by index (comparator (|g|,idx)) on BOTH the device sort AND the oracle's perm builder (keep supergrok2_sm90.cuh:1642 in lock-step) -> deterministic + A/A/A-clean by construction. Add key/index scratch (+2*Nmax) to sg2_ws_stride (opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:425) + carve. Add a tie-probe sub-test.
6	2. COMPOSE the meta-net into the model megakernel (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh, guard `if constexpr (Opt==SuperGrok2)`): after P2 reduce + B2 -> add SuperGrok2 to the P2.4 SAM guard (:546-547, REUSE — it writes st.sharpness=(g_sam-g)^2 and restores params); stage meta weights to smem (sg2_stage_weights); segmented sort (STAGE -1) from the fresh grad; inline sg2_meta_stages per tensor INSTEAD of apply_optimizer (drain the reset queue; drop the standalone's trailing bar.sync). Workspace: append dec_tc_sg2_floats as the LAST term (carve-last => 6 green cells byte-identical).
7	3. WIRE sharpness: point sg2_meta_stages' sharp_base at st.sharpness (the SAM-written (g_sam-g)^2); drop the external sharpness_packed arg on the fused path.
8	4. ROUTING: dispatch.cpp wgmma_tail_opt_id supergrok2 -> 10 (was -1, :621); mega_{decoder,vit}_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu add `case OptId::SuperGrok2` + bind the FULL SG2 state [m|v|mu|slow|gru_state(total*GH)|loss|sharpness|perm|unsort|meta-bundle|per-tensor-scalars] + bump min_state; dispatch.py add (transformer_decoder/vit, supergrok2) to _FUSED_L3_REAL(:667) + _L3_WGMMA_CELLS(:1411) + fused_train_step do_sam cadence + SG2 scalars. Route SG2 through the TC launcher, NOT the surrogate mega_vit_supergrok2.cu (surrogate model, not the race path). NOTE: per-tensor scalars (alpha/gru_decay/lamb/betas, opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:301-312) DON'T fit the global FusedScalars — thread per-tensor scalar BUFFERS via state/workspace (same wall grokadamw's per-tensor clip hit).
9	
10	## ViT: near-mechanical twin (fused_vit_megakernel.cuh, same recipe + launcher case).
11	## Mamba: LAND DORMANT (code-present, gated OUT of _L3_WGMMA_CELLS) — SAM double-forward + segmented sort re-trips the shared-mamba-forward A/A/A race (like mamba×prodigy, dispatch.py:788-805). Don't route until the in-progress race fix lands + A/A/A confirmed.
12	
13	## HONEST CAVEAT — won't grok (blocks grok, NOT single-step parity)
14	In-kernel CSA lightning-indexer keeps qI/kI in low-rank indexer_rank space, DROPS idx_UQ, scores /sqrt(rank) (supergrok2.h:217-229, :493-512; idx_UQ void :510). The fp64 bilevel ORACLE lifts qI to full d via idx_UQ + /sqrt(d) (supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h:156-157). So the kernel diverges from the eager-TRAINED net for N>64. RESULT: single-step parity vs the per-op oracle (ops.supergrok2_batched_step — uses the SAME low-rank indexer, internally consistent) is ACHIEVABLE; GROKKING is NOT (needs idx_UQ + /sqrt(d) restored — separate fix, out of scope). Gate includes an N>64 CSA fidelity PROBE that REPORTS the divergence (not a regression).
15	
16	## Gate plan
17	(B1) single-step: TC megakernel vs ops.supergrok2_batched_step, max|Δ{param,m,v,mu,slow,gru_state}| < 1e-5 (GRU/PEER hand-dot vs cuBLAS fp32-reorder tol, not 1e-12). (B2) 200-step trajectory < 1e-5. fp64 ~3e-5 fp32-storage. A/A/A bit-determinism (decoder/vit expected clean via the index-tie-break sort; mamba flagged). N>64 CSA fidelity probe (report divergence vs the bilevel oracle's full-d indexer). Single-source: all device blocks called from supergrok2.h / adjoint from supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h.
18	
19	## Top risks
20	1. Sort tie-semantics (HIGHEST) — strategy A + lock-step oracle perm builder + tie probe. Wrong => silent CSA/HCA drift over the trajectory.
21	2. Occupancy/smem — SG2's ~9KB bundle + decoder DecActs/dW/SAM scratch; re-measure regs/smem, occupancy>=1 or the GridBarrier hangs.
22	3. Per-tensor scalars don't fit FusedScalars — thread buffers via state/workspace.
23	4. N>64 grok gap — scope honesty (single-step parity yes, grok no).
24	5. Mamba A/A/A race — land dormant.
25	6. State sizing — bump launcher min_state for SG2's large persisted block.

1	#ifndef SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_STAGE_SUPERGROK2_CUH_
2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_STAGE_SUPERGROK2_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh — SuperGrok2's FULL CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU
5	// meta-net as IN-KERNEL STAGES of ONE persistent megakernel (Phase 3 of
6	// COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md: "SuperGrok2's CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta as in-kernel
7	// stages").
8	//
9	// WHAT THIS REPLACES
10	// ------------------
11	// The parity-validated per-op path (grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/
12	// supergrok2_sm90.cuh :: csa_hca_step_one) runs the SG2 meta-net as ~15-20
13	// SEPARATE kernel launches PER PARAMETER TENSOR per optimizer step:
14	//   input_proj+sort | csa: project_q, compress_k, compress_v, win_k, win_v,
15	//   indexer_q, indexer_k, topk, attention, out_proj | hca: project_q,
16	//   compress_k, compress_v, win_k, win_v, attention, out_proj | matrix-GRU
17	//   (host ATen mm×3) | PEER routing+experts (host ATen) | sg2_apply.
18	// This header collapses ALL of that into ONE persistent kernel whose stages are
19	// separated only by in-kernel grid barriers — ZERO intermediate launches and
20	// ZERO HBM round-trips for the meta tensors (the whole meta weight bundle is
21	// 35.3 KB of fp32 with the defaults — dominated by the 144-expert codebook —
22	// and is staged ONCE into shared memory, re-read zero times across all stages
23	// and all parameter tensors).
24	//
25	// THE MATH IS UNCHANGED. Every device building block here is called VERBATIM
26	// from csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h (sg2_input_proj_sort, sg2_csa_compress_kv,
27	// sg2_hca_compress_kv, sg2_csa_index_score, sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate,
28	// sg2_softmax_finalize, sg2_apply_step). The deliverable is LAUNCH-ELIMINATION,
29	// not a math change — the structure mirrors csa_hca_step_one stage-for-stage.
30	//
31	// THE SORT (honesty rail #5 — read this)
32	// --------------------------------------
33	// csa_hca_step_one sorts the per-tensor sequence by |grad| ASCENDING via a HOST
34	// torch::sort (grokking_optimizers/.../supergrok2_sm90.cuh:1642 `sort_keys.sort
35	// (0, descending=false)`). There is NO device sort kernel anywhere in the repo
36	// (verified). A global device sort would ALSO be wrong here: SG2 attention is
37	// per-tensor (each flat grad vector is its own length-N sequence; the
38	// task-queue processes many tensors), so a single sort over the packed param
39	// buffer would cross tensor boundaries. The sort is therefore left as ONE
40	// explicit pre-kernel step (a batched torch.argsort per tensor in the Python
41	// driver — see INTEGRATION-NOTES.md) producing `perm`/`unsort` index buffers
42	// the kernel consumes. Everything else is launch-free.
43	//
44	//   LAUNCH COUNT, per parameter tensor, per step:
45	//     before:  ~15-20 kernel launches  (+ host ATen mm/topk dispatches)
46	//     after:    1 argsort prep  +  1 persistent kernel   (whole batch of
47	//               tensors in the single persistent kernel via the task queue;
48	//               the argsort prep is ONE batched torch call for ALL tensors)
49	//
50	//   PATH TO ZERO EXTRA LAUNCHES: a device segmented-sort stage (bitonic over
51	//   each tensor's [N] keys, transcribed as barrier-separated passes) would fold
52	//   the sort in too. N here is tiny (a tensor's element count; the largest
53	//   race param is ~1e5) so an in-CTA bitonic per segment is feasible but is a
54	//   SEPARATE, larger piece of work; this pass does the honest maximal
55	//   elimination of everything else and flags the sort explicitly. The kernel
56	//   below is written so the sort stage can be dropped in as STAGE -1 (it only
57	//   needs `perm`/`unsort` populated before STAGE 0) with no other change.
58	//
59	// STAGE / BARRIER LAYOUT (per the decoder megakernel's discipline)
60	// ----------------------------------------------------------------
61	// gridDim.x = #SMs (one persistent CTA/SM), 256 thr/CTA. The whole step runs in
62	// ONE kernel. Because SG2 is PER-TENSOR (a tensor's attention couples only its
63	// own N rows), each CTA processes a DISJOINT set of WHOLE tensors pulled from
64	// the task queue and runs the ENTIRE per-tensor pipeline CTA-locally — so the
65	// only cross-CTA coupling is the task queue itself, and NO grid barrier is
66	// needed BETWEEN the meta stages (they are all within one CTA's tensor). The
67	// stages are sequenced by data dependence inside one CTA:
68	//
69	//   (per tensor t this CTA owns, looped over the task queue)
70	//   S0  input projection + |grad| key  (sg2_input_proj_sort, per element)   →
71	//       x_out[N,d], and gather x_sorted[N,d] = x_out[perm] using the
72	//       pre-computed `perm`.  [CTA-local, grid-stride over N]
73	//   S1  CSA context:
74	//        a. project q  = x_sorted @ q_W                                     →
75	//        b. compress c_k,c_v  (sg2_csa_compress_kv weighted pool + proj)    →
76	//        c. window  win_k,win_v = x_sorted @ {k_W,v_W}                      →
77	//        d. indexer qI = x_sorted@idx_DQ ; kI = pooled(x_sorted)@idx_K      →
78	//        e. top-k select (sg2_csa_index_score + insertion sort, per query)  →
79	//        f. attention (sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate over sel∪window)  →
80	//        g. out proj  csa_ctx = concat_heads @ out_W                         |
81	//   S2  HCA context (same shape; dense over all Nh + window, no indexer)     |
82	//   S3  matrix-GRU forward (z,r,h̃,h_new) per element, from
83	//        gru_input=[g,s,csa_ctx,hca_ctx]⊕h_old  → new_gru[N,gru_hidden];
84	//        write new_gru back to gru_state IN ORIGINAL order via `unsort`.     |
85	//   S4  PEER routing + experts (per head: query, product-key top-k of A & B,
86	//        k×k Cartesian, softmax(×10) weights, per-element expert MLP, head
87	//        average) → expert_out_sorted[N]; *= rescale.                       |
88	//   S5  unsort expert_out to original order, then sg2_apply_step per element
89	//        (smart_grad = g + alpha·mu_new + lamb_eff·slow_new, then Adam tail).
90	//
91	// Everything S0..S5 for one tensor is CTA-local; the per-tensor intermediates
92	// live in a caller-provided per-CTA workspace (sized for the largest tensor),
93	// re-used tensor to tensor. There is exactly ONE grid barrier in the kernel:
94	// after the whole task-queue drains, so the queue can be reset for a composing
95	// model stage if this tail is fused after a model bwd (see the launcher).
96	//
97	// DESIGN CHOICE — tensor-per-CTA (a CONSCIOUS divergence from design req #1)
98	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
99	// Design req #1 asked for "CTAs partitioning the element/sequence space, ONE
100	// grid barrier between stages with cross-CTA dependencies (the sort and the
101	// attention windows are the couplings)" — i.e. ONE tensor at a time spread
102	// across the WHOLE grid, with a grid barrier after compress so all compressed
103	// K/V are ready before attention/topk. This header instead puts a WHOLE tensor
104	// on ONE CTA (the meta stages become __syncthreads-separated, no grid barrier
105	// between them), because SG2 attention couples only a tensor's OWN N rows — so
106	// the only genuine cross-CTA coupling is the task queue, and tensor-per-CTA is
107	// correct + far simpler + barrier-light.
108	//   THE COST (own it, don't hide it — honesty rails): with ~30 param tensors and
109	//   ~130 SMs, ONE 256-thread CTA does each tensor's entire CSA/HCA attention
110	//   (HCA is dense, ~N·Nh·heads·head_dim), and ~100 CTAs pull an empty queue and
111	//   idle at the final barrier. The per-LAUNCH path it replaces spread each
112	//   tensor's attention across the full grid, so this trades intra-tensor
113	//   parallelism for launch-elimination. That is a deliberate CORRECTNESS-FIRST
114	//   choice for this pass; the perf follow-up is exactly req #1's design —
115	//   sequence-space partitioning of the LARGE tensors with a grid barrier after
116	//   compress (the small tensors, which dominate the race's param count, are fine
117	//   on one CTA). The stages here are written so that refactor reuses the SAME
118	//   stage bodies (they already take explicit N/Nc/Nh and CTA-cooperative loops);
119	//   only the OUTER driver (who owns which rows) changes. See the report.
120	//
121	// DETERMINISM
122	// -----------
123	// No float atomics anywhere. Every reduction (projection dot products,
124	// attention online-softmax, expert MLP, GRU gates) is computed by a SINGLE
125	// owner thread for its output element in a FIXED accumulation order — the
126	// owner-computes pattern proven in the decoder cell (fused_decoder_megakernel
127	// .cuh P2) and F3's MoE-bwd. Each output element [row, channel] (or [row] for
128	// the experts/apply) is owned by one thread via a grid-stride loop; that thread
129	// does the full inner reduction itself. Across tensors there is no sharing — the
130	// result is deterministic (run-to-run identical) regardless of CTA scheduling.
131	//
132	// PARITY (NOT bit-identity) vs csa_hca_step_one
133	// ---------------------------------------------
134	// This matches csa_hca_step_one to fp32 round-off (the 1e-5 GPU parity target),
135	// NOT bit-for-bit. Two stages are the parity HOTSPOTS the gate should watch:
136	//   * matrix-GRU (S3) and PEER routing (S4): the reference computes these with
137	//     cuBLAS/ATen (torch::mm/matmul, torch::sigmoid/tanh/softmax). Here they are
138	//     hand-written sequential dot products + expf/tanhf. Accurate transcendentals
139	//     are used (expf, NOT ptx_expf) precisely so the only residual is FP
140	//     reduction ORDER (sequential vs cuBLAS tiling) — fp32 round-off, well within
141	//     1e-5. The CSA/HCA attention + compress stages, by contrast, DO use ptx_expf
142	//     because the reference kernels (sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate,
143	//     sg2_csa_compress_kv) use ptx_expf — matching them there is correct.
144	//   * PEER top-k uses descending insertion sort; the reference uses torch::topk.
145	//     Identical for distinct scores; tie-order is unspecified in both (low risk).
146	// The per-element apply (S5) calls sg2_apply_step verbatim — bit-identical there.
147	//

153	// the bundle once before the call; see INTEGRATION-NOTES.md). A bf16-COMPUTE
154	// follow-up would be a flag defaulting to THIS fp32 path, exactly like the
155	// decoder cell's bf16 TODO — see the report.

175	// ── Compile-time dims (defaults = supergrok2.py constructor + OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS).
176	//    Templated so a third project can instantiate other shapes; the race uses the
177	//    defaults. These bound the per-CTA shared/workspace footprint. ──────────────
178	template <
179	    int D_MODEL    = 8,    // input_proj out / attention model dim
180	    int NUM_HEADS  = 2,    // attention heads  (head_dim = D_MODEL/NUM_HEADS = 4)
181	    int GRU_HIDDEN = 4,    // MiniGRU hidden  (per-element carried state width)
182	    int NUM_EXPERTS = 144, // PEER expert codebook size (pk_dim = sqrt = 12)
183	    int EXPERT_HIDDEN = 16,// per-element expert MLP hidden width
184	    int NUM_PEER_HEADS = 4,// PEER routing heads (averaged)
185	    int PEER_TOPK  = 4,    // top-k per product-key axis (k×k experts/head)
186	    int CSA_COMPRESS = 4,  // CSA pooling stride m
187	    int CSA_WINDOW = 8,    // CSA pool width / sliding-window W
188	    int CSA_TOPK   = 16,   // CSA indexer top-k compressed entries
189	    int HCA_COMPRESS = 128,// HCA pooling stride m'
190	    int INDEXER_RANK = 4   // lightning-indexer low rank
191	>
192	struct SG2Dims {
193	    static constexpr int d_model      = D_MODEL;
194	    static constexpr int num_heads    = NUM_HEADS;
195	    static constexpr int head_dim     = D_MODEL / NUM_HEADS;
196	    static constexpr int gru_hidden   = GRU_HIDDEN;
197	    static constexpr int num_experts  = NUM_EXPERTS;
198	    static constexpr int expert_hidden = EXPERT_HIDDEN;
199	    static constexpr int num_peer_heads = NUM_PEER_HEADS;
200	    static constexpr int peer_topk    = PEER_TOPK;
201	    static constexpr int csa_compress = CSA_COMPRESS;
202	    static constexpr int csa_window   = CSA_WINDOW;
203	    static constexpr int csa_topk     = CSA_TOPK;
204	    static constexpr int hca_compress = HCA_COMPRESS;
205	    static constexpr int indexer_rank = INDEXER_RANK;
206	    static constexpr int pk_dim       = 12;  // sqrt(144); static for the default
207	    static constexpr int gru_in       = 2 + 2 * D_MODEL;          // [g,s,csa,hca]
208	    static constexpr int peer_in      = GRU_HIDDEN + 2 * D_MODEL + 2;
209	};

211	// ── The SG2 meta weight bundle — fp32 pointers, staged ONCE into shared memory
212	//    at the top of the kernel and re-read zero times from HBM across all stages
213	//    and all tensors. Layout matches the per-op path's tensors (row-major). The
214	//    bundle, with the supergrok2.py defaults, is 9028 fp32 = 35.3 KB:
215	//      input_proj 8*2+8 = 24 ; csa q/k/v/out 4*64 = 256 ; compress_w 8 ;
216	//      idx_DQ/idx_K 2*(8*4) = 64 ; hca q/k/v/out 4*64 = 256 ;
217	//      gru Wz/Wr/Wh 3*(4*26) + b 3*4 = 324  (xin = gru_in+gru_hidden = 22+4 = 26);
218	//      peer Wq 4*(8*22) = 704 ; prod A/B 2*4*(12*4) = 384 ;
219	//      experts W1/b1/W2 3*(144*16) + b2 144 = 7056.
220	//    35.3 KB < the 48 KB static smem cap (and below the decoder cell's ~42 KB),
221	//    so dynamicSMemBytes=0 and the occupancy>=1 guard hold. The expert codebook
222	//    (7056 of 9028 floats) dominates — staging it in smem ONCE is the residency
223	//    win (every PEER lookup reads it, across all stages and all tensors). NOTE:
224	//    this 35.3 KB is the SMEM-resident copy; with the per-thread scratch (topk
225	//    16+16 ints/thread; peer/gru ~40-78 floats/thread) the kernel is smem- AND
226	//    register-heavy — occupancy is checked at launch (refuse if < 1 block/SM),
227	//    exactly the decoder cell's hang-freedom contract. ─────────────────────────
228	struct SG2Weights {
229	    // input projection (proj_W is [d_model, 2] row-major, proj_b [d_model])
230	    const float* input_proj_W;
231	    const float* input_proj_b;
232	    // CSA projections ([d_model,d_model] row-major) + pooling logits + indexer
233	    const float* csa_q_W;
234	    const float* csa_k_W;
235	    const float* csa_v_W;
236	    const float* csa_out_W;
237	    const float* csa_compress_w;   // [csa_window]
238	    const float* csa_idx_DQ;       // [d_model, indexer_rank]
239	    const float* csa_idx_K;        // [d_model, indexer_rank]
240	    // HCA projections ([d_model,d_model])
241	    const float* hca_q_W;
242	    const float* hca_k_W;
243	    const float* hca_v_W;
244	    const float* hca_out_W;
245	    // matrix-GRU weights (nn.Linear .weight [out=gru_hidden, in=gru_in+gru_hidden])
246	    const float* gru_Wz;  const float* gru_bz;
247	    const float* gru_Wr;  const float* gru_br;
248	    const float* gru_Wh;  const float* gru_bh;
249	    // PEER routing: stacked per head
250	    const float* peer_query_Ws;    // [num_peer_heads, d_model, peer_in]
251	    const float* prod_keys_A;      // [num_peer_heads, pk_dim, d_model/2]
252	    const float* prod_keys_B;      // [num_peer_heads, pk_dim, d_model/2]
253	    // per-element expert MLP (shared codebook, indexed)
254	    const float* expert_W1;        // [num_experts, expert_hidden]
255	    const float* expert_b1;        // [num_experts, expert_hidden]
256	    const float* expert_W2;        // [num_experts, expert_hidden]
257	    const float* expert_b2;        // [num_experts]
258	};

260	// ── Per-tensor sequence-attention state ABI. The packed flat buffers carry ALL
261	//    parameter tensors back-to-back; tensor t occupies rows [row_off[t],
262	//    row_off[t]+n[t]). The per-CTA workspace is sized for the LARGEST tensor's
263	//    intermediates and re-used per tensor. The sort index buffers (perm/unsort)
264	//    are PRE-COMPUTED by the Python driver (the one explicit pre-kernel step).
265	struct SG2State {
266	    // Per-element optimizer state (packed across all tensors, element-indexed).
267	    float* exp_avg;        // [total]  Adam m
268	    float* exp_avg_sq;     // [total]  Adam v
269	    float* mu;             // [total]  expert-output EMA  (sg2_apply_step mu_state)
270	    float* slow;           // [total]  slow-gradient EMA  (grokfast)
271	    // Per-element matrix-GRU carried hidden state, ROW-major [total, gru_hidden].
272	    float* gru_state;      // [total * gru_hidden]
273	    // Pre-computed sort permutations, per tensor, ELEMENT-indexed into [0,n[t]).
274	    //   perm[row_off[t]+i]   = source row in ORIGINAL order for the i-th SORTED row
275	    //   unsort[row_off[t]+i] = sorted-row position of original row i
276	    const int* perm;       // [total]
277	    const int* unsort;     // [total]
278	    // Per-CTA scratch workspace (the meta intermediates, re-used per tensor).
279	    //   layout per CTA (floats), Nmax = max tensor numel:
280	    //     x_sorted   : Nmax * d_model
281	    //     csa_ctx    : Nmax * d_model
282	    //     hca_ctx    : Nmax * d_model
283	    //     q/c_k/c_v/win_k/win_v (csa): 5 * Nmax * d_model  (reused for hca)
284	    //     qI         : Nmax * indexer_rank
285	    //     kI         : ceil(Nmax/csa_compress) * indexer_rank
286	    //     sel        : Nmax * max(csa_topk,1)   (int, aliased in the float buf)
287	    //     concat     : Nmax * d_model
288	    //     new_gru    : Nmax * gru_hidden
289	    //     expert_out : Nmax
290	    //   The host computes the per-CTA stride (floats) and passes it as ws_stride.
291	    float* workspace;      // [n_ctas * ws_stride]
292	    int64_t ws_stride;     // floats per CTA
293	    int     n_tensors;     // == ctx.n_tasks
294	    const int*     n;          // [n_tensors] element counts
295	    const int64_t* row_off;    // [n_tensors] start element of each tensor
296	};

361	// Cooperative copy [src -> dst) of `n` floats by the whole CTA.
362	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_smem_load(
363	    float* __restrict__ dst, const float* __restrict__ src, int n) {
364	    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) dst[i] = src[i];

399	// =====================================================================
400	//  Per-CTA workspace accessor. Carves the per-tensor intermediate
401	//  pointers out of this CTA's slice of the flat workspace. Layout MUST
402	//  match the host's ws_stride computation (sg2_ws_stride below).
403	// =====================================================================
404	template <typename Dims>
405	struct SG2Work {
406	    float* x_sorted;   // [N, d_model]
407	    float* csa_ctx;    // [N, d_model]
408	    float* hca_ctx;    // [N, d_model]
409	    float* q;          // [N, d_model]  (scratch, reused csa/hca)
410	    float* c_k;        // [Ncmax, d_model]
411	    float* c_v;        // [Ncmax, d_model]
412	    float* win_k;      // [N, d_model]
413	    float* win_v;      // [N, d_model]
414	    float* qI;         // [N, indexer_rank]
415	    float* kI;         // [Ncmax, indexer_rank]
416	    int*   sel;        // [N, max(csa_topk,1)]  (int view)
417	    float* concat;     // [N, d_model]
418	    float* new_gru;    // [N, gru_hidden]
419	    float* expert_out; // [N]
420	};
421	
422	// floats-per-CTA stride. Conservatively sized for the LARGEST tensor (Nmax) so
423	// the same slice serves every tensor. Ncmax = ceil(Nmax/csa_compress) bounds the
424	// compressed buffers (csa stride 4 is the smallest, so it dominates over hca).
425	template <typename Dims>
426	__host__ __device__ inline int64_t sg2_ws_stride(int64_t Nmax) {
427	    const int64_t d = Dims::d_model;
428	    const int64_t rk = Dims::indexer_rank;
429	    const int64_t gh = Dims::gru_hidden;
430	    const int64_t Ncmax = (Nmax + Dims::csa_compress - 1) / Dims::csa_compress;
431	    const int64_t topk = (Dims::csa_topk > 1) ? Dims::csa_topk : 1;
432	    int64_t f = 0;
433	    f += Nmax * d;          // x_sorted
434	    f += Nmax * d;          // csa_ctx
435	    f += Nmax * d;          // hca_ctx
436	    f += Nmax * d;          // q
437	    f += Ncmax * d;         // c_k
438	    f += Ncmax * d;         // c_v
439	    f += Nmax * d;          // win_k
440	    f += Nmax * d;          // win_v
441	    f += Nmax * rk;         // qI
442	    f += Ncmax * rk;        // kI
443	    f += Nmax * topk;       // sel (int, 1 float each)
444	    f += Nmax * d;          // concat
445	    f += Nmax * gh;         // new_gru
446	    f += Nmax;              // expert_out
447	    return f;
448	}
449	
450	template <typename Dims>
451	__device__ __forceinline__ SG2Work<Dims> sg2_carve_ws(
452	    float* base, int64_t Nmax) {
453	    const int64_t d = Dims::d_model;
454	    const int64_t rk = Dims::indexer_rank;
455	    const int64_t gh = Dims::gru_hidden;
456	    const int64_t Ncmax = (Nmax + Dims::csa_compress - 1) / Dims::csa_compress;
457	    const int64_t topk = (Dims::csa_topk > 1) ? Dims::csa_topk : 1;
458	    SG2Work<Dims> ws;
459	    float* p = base;
460	    ws.x_sorted = p;   p += Nmax * d;
461	    ws.csa_ctx  = p;   p += Nmax * d;
462	    ws.hca_ctx  = p;   p += Nmax * d;
463	    ws.q        = p;   p += Nmax * d;
464	    ws.c_k      = p;   p += Ncmax * d;
465	    ws.c_v      = p;   p += Ncmax * d;
466	    ws.win_k    = p;   p += Nmax * d;
467	    ws.win_v    = p;   p += Nmax * d;
468	    ws.qI       = p;   p += Nmax * rk;
469	    ws.kI       = p;   p += Ncmax * rk;
470	    ws.sel      = reinterpret_cast<int*>(p);   p += Nmax * topk;
471	    ws.concat   = p;   p += Nmax * d;
472	    ws.new_gru  = p;   p += Nmax * gh;
473	    ws.expert_out = p; p += Nmax;
474	    return ws;
475	}

477	// =====================================================================
478	//  STAGE BODIES — each is CTA-cooperative with the owner-computes
479	//  determinism rule (one thread fully reduces each output element).
480	//  All transcribed from csa_hca_step_one's per-launch kernels; the math
481	//  building blocks are CALLED from sg::algorithms.
482	// =====================================================================
483	
484	// S0: input projection (per element) + gather sorted features.
485	// x_out is computed per ORIGINAL element i: x_out[i,:] (sg2_input_proj_sort);
486	// then x_sorted[r,:] = x_out[perm[r], :]. We FUSE: each sorted-row r reads its
487	// source original row src=perm[r], projects that row's (g,s) directly into
488	// x_sorted[r,:]. This matches csa_hca_step_one (project all, gather by perm)
489	// bit-for-bit since the projection is per-row and the gather is a pure permute.
490	template <typename Dims, typename GradT>
491	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_input_proj_sorted(
492	    const SG2SmemWeights<Dims>& w,
493	    const GradT* __restrict__ grad,   // [N] original order (tensor slice)
494	    const float* __restrict__ sharp,  // [N] original order
495	    const int* __restrict__ perm,     // [N] sorted-row -> original-row
496	    float* __restrict__ x_sorted,     // [N, d_model] out (sorted order)
497	    int N) {
498	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
499	    // CTA-local: this whole tensor is owned by ONE CTA, so the grid-stride is
500	    // blockDim.x (threads of this CTA), NOT gridDim*blockDim. One thread owns
501	    // one SORTED row r and computes all d channels (owner-computes → deterministic).
502	    for (int r = threadIdx.x; r < N; r += blockDim.x) {
503	        const int src = perm[r];
504	        float g = static_cast<float>(grad[src]);
505	        float s = sharp[src];
506	        if (!isfinite(g)) g = 0.0f;
507	        if (!isfinite(s)) s = 0.0f;
508	        #pragma unroll
509	        for (int dd = 0; dd < d; ++dd) {
510	            x_sorted[r * d + dd] =
511	                  w.input_proj_W[dd * 2]     * g
512	                + w.input_proj_W[dd * 2 + 1] * s
513	                + w.input_proj_b[dd];
514	        }
515	    }
516	}
517	
518	// Generic per-(row,channel) projection out[t,d] = sum_k W[d,k]*x[t,k].
519	// Owner thread per output element does the full dot — deterministic.
520	template <typename Dims>
521	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_project(
522	    const float* __restrict__ x,    // [N, d_model]
523	    const float* __restrict__ W,    // [d_model, d_model] row-major
524	    float* __restrict__ out,        // [N, d_model]
525	    int N) {
526	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
527	    const int total = N * d;
528	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += blockDim.x) {
529	        const int t = idx / d;
530	        const int oc = idx % d;
531	        float acc = 0.0f;
532	        #pragma unroll
533	        for (int k = 0; k < d; ++k)
534	            acc += W[oc * d + k] * x[t * d + k];
535	        out[idx] = acc;
536	    }
537	}

539	// CSA/HCA compressed K or V (weighted pool then project, fused per (j,channel)).
540	// Mirrors csa_compress_kv_kernel / hca_compress_kv_kernel. is_csa selects the
541	// pool helper + compress_w; hca uses mean (hca_w=nullptr) at stride hca_compress.
542	template <typename Dims, bool IsCsa>
543	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_compress(
544	    const float* __restrict__ x_sorted,   // [N, d_model]
545	    const float* __restrict__ proj_W,      // [d_model, d_model]
546	    const float* __restrict__ compress_w,  // [csa_window] (csa) or unused (hca)
547	    float* __restrict__ c_out,             // [Nc, d_model]
548	    int N, int Nc) {
549	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
550	    const int total = Nc * d;
551	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += blockDim.x) {
552	        const int j = idx / d;
553	        const int oc = idx % d;
554	        float acc = 0.0f;
555	        #pragma unroll
556	        for (int k = 0; k < d; ++k) {
557	            float pooled;
558	            if (IsCsa) {
559	                pooled = sg2alg::sg2_csa_compress_kv<float>(
560	                    x_sorted, compress_w, j, k,
561	                    (int64_t)N, d, Dims::csa_compress, Dims::csa_window);
562	            } else {
563	                pooled = sg2alg::sg2_hca_compress_kv<float>(
564	                    x_sorted, /*hca_w=*/nullptr, j, k,
565	                    (int64_t)N, d, Dims::hca_compress);
566	            }
567	            acc += proj_W[oc * d + k] * pooled;
568	        }
569	        c_out[idx] = acc;
570	    }
571	}

573	// Indexer query qI[t,r] = sum_m x[t,m]*idx_DQ[m,r]. Owner per (t,r).
574	template <typename Dims>
575	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_indexer_q(
576	    const float* __restrict__ x_sorted,  // [N, d_model]
577	    const float* __restrict__ idx_DQ,    // [d_model, rank]
578	    float* __restrict__ qI,              // [N, rank]
579	    int N) {
580	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
581	    constexpr int rk = Dims::indexer_rank;
582	    const int total = N * rk;
583	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += blockDim.x) {
584	        const int t = idx / rk;
585	        const int r = idx % rk;
586	        float acc = 0.0f;
587	        #pragma unroll
588	        for (int m = 0; m < d; ++m)
589	            acc += x_sorted[t * d + m] * idx_DQ[m * rk + r];
590	        qI[idx] = acc;
591	    }
592	}

594	// Indexer key kI[s,r] = sum_m pooled_csa(x,s,m)*idx_K[m,r]. Owner per (s,r).
595	template <typename Dims>
596	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_indexer_k(
597	    const float* __restrict__ x_sorted,  // [N, d_model]
598	    const float* __restrict__ idx_K,     // [d_model, rank]
599	    const float* __restrict__ compress_w,// [csa_window]
600	    float* __restrict__ kI,              // [Nc, rank]
601	    int N, int Nc) {
602	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
603	    constexpr int rk = Dims::indexer_rank;
604	    const int total = Nc * rk;
605	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += blockDim.x) {
606	        const int s = idx / rk;
607	        const int r = idx % rk;
608	        float acc = 0.0f;
609	        #pragma unroll
610	        for (int m = 0; m < d; ++m) {
611	            const float pooled = sg2alg::sg2_csa_compress_kv<float>(
612	                x_sorted, compress_w, s, m,
613	                (int64_t)N, d, Dims::csa_compress, Dims::csa_window);
614	            acc += pooled * idx_K[m * rk + r];
615	        }
616	        kI[idx] = acc;
617	    }
618	}

620	// CSA indexer top-k: per query t, score all Nc compressed entries, keep top-K by
621	// descending insertion (matches csa_indexer_topk_kernel exactly). Owner per query.
622	// Uses a small per-thread register array (CSA_TOPK<=64, the algo max bound).
623	template <typename Dims>
624	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_topk(
625	    const float* __restrict__ qI,   // [N, rank]
626	    const float* __restrict__ kI,   // [Nc, rank]
627	    int* __restrict__ sel,          // [N, topk]
628	    int N, int Nc, int topk) {
629	    constexpr int rk = Dims::indexer_rank;
630	    const int K = (topk < Dims::csa_topk) ? topk : Dims::csa_topk;
631	    for (int t = threadIdx.x; t < N; t += blockDim.x) {
632	        float best_score[Dims::csa_topk];
633	        int   best_idx[Dims::csa_topk];
634	        #pragma unroll
635	        for (int i = 0; i < Dims::csa_topk; ++i) {
636	            best_score[i] = -INFINITY; best_idx[i] = -1;
637	        }
638	        const float* q = qI + t * rk;
639	        for (int s = 0; s < Nc; ++s) {
640	            const float sc = sg2alg::sg2_csa_index_score(q, kI + s * rk, rk);
641	            if (sc > best_score[K - 1]) {
642	                int p = K - 1;
643	                while (p > 0 && best_score[p - 1] < sc) {
644	                    best_score[p] = best_score[p - 1];
645	                    best_idx[p]   = best_idx[p - 1];
646	                    --p;
647	                }
648	                best_score[p] = sc;
649	                best_idx[p]   = s;
650	            }
651	        }
652	        for (int i = 0; i < K; ++i) sel[t * topk + i] = best_idx[i];
653	    }
654	}

656	// CSA attention: per (query t, head h) online-softmax over selected compressed
657	// entries ∪ causal window. Owner thread per (t,h); writes head slice into concat.
658	// Mirrors csa_attention_kernel (acc kept per-thread; bit-identical adds).
659	template <typename Dims>
660	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_csa_attention(
661	    const float* __restrict__ q,      // [N, d_model]
662	    const float* __restrict__ c_k,    // [Nc, d_model]
663	    const float* __restrict__ c_v,    // [Nc, d_model]
664	    const float* __restrict__ win_k,  // [N, d_model]
665	    const float* __restrict__ win_v,  // [N, d_model]
666	    const int* __restrict__ sel,      // [N, topk]
667	    float* __restrict__ concat,       // [N, d_model] (head-concatenated)
668	    int N, int Nc, int topk) {
669	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
670	    constexpr int hd = Dims::head_dim;
671	    const int total = N * Dims::num_heads;
672	    const float scale = rsqrtf((float)hd);
673	    for (int gid = threadIdx.x; gid < total; gid += blockDim.x) {
674	        const int t = gid / Dims::num_heads;
675	        const int h = gid % Dims::num_heads;
676	        const int hoff = h * hd;
677	        float acc[hd];
678	        #pragma unroll
679	        for (int e = 0; e < hd; ++e) acc[e] = 0.0f;
680	        float run_max = -INFINITY, run_denom = 0.0f;
681	        const float* qv = q + t * d + hoff;
682	        for (int i = 0; i < topk; ++i) {
683	            const int s = sel[t * topk + i];
684	            if (s < 0 || s >= Nc) continue;
685	            sg2alg::sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
686	                qv, c_k + s * d + hoff, c_v + s * d + hoff,
687	                &run_max, &run_denom, acc, scale, hd);
688	        }
689	        const int w0 = (t - Dims::csa_window + 1 > 0) ? (t - Dims::csa_window + 1) : 0;
690	        for (int s = w0; s <= t; ++s) {
691	            sg2alg::sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
692	                qv, win_k + s * d + hoff, win_v + s * d + hoff,
693	                &run_max, &run_denom, acc, scale, hd);
694	        }
695	        sg2alg::sg2_softmax_finalize(acc, run_denom, hd);
696	        #pragma unroll
697	        for (int e = 0; e < hd; ++e) concat[t * d + hoff + e] = acc[e];
698	    }
699	}

701	// HCA attention: dense over all Nh compressed entries ∪ window (no top-k).
702	template <typename Dims>
703	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_hca_attention(
704	    const float* __restrict__ q,      // [N, d_model]
705	    const float* __restrict__ c_k,    // [Nh, d_model]
706	    const float* __restrict__ c_v,    // [Nh, d_model]
707	    const float* __restrict__ win_k,  // [N, d_model]
708	    const float* __restrict__ win_v,  // [N, d_model]
709	    float* __restrict__ concat,       // [N, d_model]
710	    int N, int Nh) {
711	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
712	    constexpr int hd = Dims::head_dim;
713	    const int total = N * Dims::num_heads;
714	    const float scale = rsqrtf((float)hd);
715	    for (int gid = threadIdx.x; gid < total; gid += blockDim.x) {
716	        const int t = gid / Dims::num_heads;
717	        const int h = gid % Dims::num_heads;
718	        const int hoff = h * hd;
719	        float acc[hd];
720	        #pragma unroll
721	        for (int e = 0; e < hd; ++e) acc[e] = 0.0f;
722	        float run_max = -INFINITY, run_denom = 0.0f;
723	        const float* qv = q + t * d + hoff;
724	        for (int s = 0; s < Nh; ++s) {
725	            sg2alg::sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
726	                qv, c_k + s * d + hoff, c_v + s * d + hoff,
727	                &run_max, &run_denom, acc, scale, hd);
728	        }
729	        const int w0 = (t - Dims::csa_window + 1 > 0) ? (t - Dims::csa_window + 1) : 0;
730	        for (int s = w0; s <= t; ++s) {
731	            sg2alg::sg2_attention_score_and_accumulate(
732	                qv, win_k + s * d + hoff, win_v + s * d + hoff,
733	                &run_max, &run_denom, acc, scale, hd);
734	        }
735	        sg2alg::sg2_softmax_finalize(acc, run_denom, hd);
736	        #pragma unroll
737	        for (int e = 0; e < hd; ++e) concat[t * d + hoff + e] = acc[e];

741	// Out projection: ctx[t,d] = sum_k out_W[d,k]*concat[t,k]. (== sg2_stage_project)
742	template <typename Dims>
743	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_out_proj(
744	    const float* __restrict__ concat, const float* __restrict__ out_W,

749	// Matrix-GRU forward (per element row). gru_input = [g, s, csa_ctx, hca_ctx]
750	// (all in SORTED order); h_old = gru_state[src] in sorted order (src=perm[r]).
751	//   z = sigmoid(xh @ Wz.T + bz), r = sigmoid(xh @ Wr.T + br),
752	//   h̃ = tanh(xrh @ Wh.T + bh),  h_new = (1-z)*h_old + z*h̃
753	// Owner thread per sorted row r computes the whole gru_hidden vector. The new
754	// state is written back to gru_state in ORIGINAL order (gru_state[src]).
755	template <typename Dims>
756	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_gru(
757	    const SG2SmemWeights<Dims>& w,
758	    const float* __restrict__ g_sorted,   // [N]
759	    const float* __restrict__ s_sorted,   // [N]
760	    const float* __restrict__ csa_ctx,    // [N, d_model] (sorted)
761	    const float* __restrict__ hca_ctx,    // [N, d_model] (sorted)
762	    const int* __restrict__ perm,         // [N] sorted-row -> original-row
763	    float* __restrict__ gru_state,        // [N, gru_hidden] ORIGINAL order (in/out)
764	    float* __restrict__ new_gru,          // [N, gru_hidden] SORTED order (out)
765	    int N) {
766	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
767	    constexpr int gh = Dims::gru_hidden;
768	    constexpr int gi = Dims::gru_in;        // 2 + 2*d
769	    constexpr int xin = gi + gh;            // concat width into the gates
770	    for (int r = threadIdx.x; r < N; r += blockDim.x) {
771	        const int src = perm[r];
772	        // Build gru_input row [g, s, csa(d), hca(d)] and h_old.
773	        float xin_buf[xin];
774	        xin_buf[0] = g_sorted[r];
775	        xin_buf[1] = s_sorted[r];
776	        #pragma unroll
777	        for (int k = 0; k < d; ++k) xin_buf[2 + k]     = csa_ctx[r * d + k];
778	        #pragma unroll
779	        for (int k = 0; k < d; ++k) xin_buf[2 + d + k] = hca_ctx[r * d + k];
780	        float h_old[gh];
781	        #pragma unroll
782	        for (int k = 0; k < gh; ++k) h_old[k] = gru_state[src * gh + k];
783	        // xh = [gru_input, h_old]
784	        #pragma unroll
785	        for (int k = 0; k < gh; ++k) xin_buf[gi + k] = h_old[k];
786	        // z, r gates: linear over xh (Wz/Wr are [gh, xin] row-major).
787	        float zg[gh], rg[gh];
788	        #pragma unroll
789	        for (int o = 0; o < gh; ++o) {
790	            float az = w.gru_bz[o], ar = w.gru_br[o];
791	            #pragma unroll
792	            for (int k = 0; k < xin; ++k) {
793	                az += w.gru_Wz[o * xin + k] * xin_buf[k];
794	                ar += w.gru_Wr[o * xin + k] * xin_buf[k];
795	            }
796	            // Accurate sigmoid (expf, NOT ptx_expf): the reference matrix-GRU
797	            // (csa_hca_step_one) uses torch::sigmoid — an accurate transcendental.
798	            // Matching it with expf keeps the GRU on the reference's precision;
799	            // ptx_expf (ex2.approx) here would diverge invisibly to the fp64 mirror
800	            // and only surface at the 1e-5 GPU parity gate. (tanhf below is already
801	            // the accurate intrinsic, matching torch::tanh.)
802	            zg[o] = 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-az));
803	            rg[o] = 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-ar));
804	        }
805	        // xrh = [gru_input, r*h_old]; overwrite the h_old tail with r*h_old.
806	        #pragma unroll
807	        for (int k = 0; k < gh; ++k) xin_buf[gi + k] = rg[k] * h_old[k];
808	        // h̃ = tanh(xrh @ Wh.T + bh), then h_new = (1-z)*h_old + z*h̃.
809	        #pragma unroll
810	        for (int o = 0; o < gh; ++o) {
811	            float ah = w.gru_bh[o];
812	            #pragma unroll
813	            for (int k = 0; k < xin; ++k) ah += w.gru_Wh[o * xin + k] * xin_buf[k];
814	            const float ht = tanhf(ah);
815	            const float hn = (1.0f - zg[o]) * h_old[o] + zg[o] * ht;
816	            new_gru[r * gh + o] = hn;       // sorted order (feeds PEER)
817	            gru_state[src * gh + o] = hn;   // persist in ORIGINAL order
818	        }
819	    }
820	}
821	
822	// PEER routing + experts (per element row, sorted order). Mirrors
823	// detail::peer_expert_forward + the eager forward exactly:
824	//   peer_input = [new_gru, csa_ctx, hca_ctx, g, s]  (width peer_in)
825	//   per head: query = peer_input @ Wq.T (d_model wide); q_a=[:half], q_b=[half:];
826	//     sa = q_a @ A.T, sb = q_b @ B.T (each [pk_dim]); top-k of each → ka,kb;
827	//     soft = softmax(top*10); expert = a_idx*pk_dim + b_idx (k×k); routing =
828	//     soft_a⊗soft_b; per expert: ReLU MLP on scalar g; out = Σ routing*mlp;
829	//   head outputs averaged ÷ num_peer_heads; expert_out *= rescale.
830	// Owner thread per row r. The MLP input scalar is g_sorted[r] (matches eager).
831	template <typename Dims>
832	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg2_stage_peer(
833	    const SG2SmemWeights<Dims>& w,
834	    const float* __restrict__ new_gru,    // [N, gru_hidden] sorted
835	    const float* __restrict__ csa_ctx,    // [N, d_model] sorted
836	    const float* __restrict__ hca_ctx,    // [N, d_model] sorted
837	    const float* __restrict__ g_sorted,   // [N]
838	    const float* __restrict__ s_sorted,   // [N]
839	    float* __restrict__ expert_out,       // [N] sorted (out)
840	    float rescale, int N) {
841	    constexpr int d = Dims::d_model;
842	    constexpr int gh = Dims::gru_hidden;
843	    constexpr int pin = Dims::peer_in;
844	    constexpr int half = Dims::d_model / 2;
845	    constexpr int pkd = Dims::pk_dim;
846	    constexpr int K = Dims::peer_topk;
847	    const float T = 10.0f;
848	    for (int r = threadIdx.x; r < N; r += blockDim.x) {
849	        // Build peer_input row.
850	        float pin_buf[pin];
851	        int o = 0;
852	        #pragma unroll
853	        for (int k = 0; k < gh; ++k) pin_buf[o++] = new_gru[r * gh + k];
854	        #pragma unroll
855	        for (int k = 0; k < d; ++k)  pin_buf[o++] = csa_ctx[r * d + k];
856	        #pragma unroll
857	        for (int k = 0; k < d; ++k)  pin_buf[o++] = hca_ctx[r * d + k];
858	        pin_buf[o++] = g_sorted[r];
859	        pin_buf[o++] = s_sorted[r];
860	
861	        const float gval = g_sorted[r];   // expert-MLP scalar input
862	        float head_sum = 0.0f;
863	        for (int h = 0; h < Dims::num_peer_heads; ++h) {
864	            const float* Wq = w.peer_query_Ws + (int64_t)h * d * pin;
865	            const float* A  = w.prod_keys_A   + (int64_t)h * pkd * half;
866	            const float* B  = w.prod_keys_B   + (int64_t)h * pkd * half;
867	            // query = Wq @ peer_input  (Wq is [d_model, peer_in] row-major).
868	            float query[d];
869	            #pragma unroll
870	            for (int oc = 0; oc < d; ++oc) {
871	                float acc = 0.0f;
872	                #pragma unroll
873	                for (int k = 0; k < pin; ++k) acc += Wq[oc * pin + k] * pin_buf[k];
874	                query[oc] = acc;
875	            }
876	            // scores_a[na] = q_a @ A.T ; scores_b[nb] = q_b @ B.T (na=nb=pk_dim).
877	            float sa[pkd], sb[pkd];
878	            #pragma unroll
879	            for (int n = 0; n < pkd; ++n) {
880	                float aa = 0.0f, bb = 0.0f;
881	                #pragma unroll
882	                for (int k = 0; k < half; ++k) {
883	                    aa += query[k]        * A[n * half + k];
884	                    bb += query[half + k] * B[n * half + k];
885	                }
886	                sa[n] = aa; sb[n] = bb;
887	            }
888	            // top-k of sa and sb (descending insertion), K = peer_topk.
889	            const int ka = (K < pkd) ? K : pkd;
890	            const int kb = ka;  // pk_dim symmetric
891	            float ta_v[K]; int ta_i[K];
892	            float tb_v[K]; int tb_i[K];
893	            #pragma unroll
894	            for (int i = 0; i < K; ++i) {
895	                ta_v[i] = -INFINITY; ta_i[i] = 0;
896	                tb_v[i] = -INFINITY; tb_i[i] = 0;
897	            }
898	            for (int n = 0; n < pkd; ++n) {
899	                if (sa[n] > ta_v[ka - 1]) {
900	                    int p = ka - 1;
901	                    while (p > 0 && ta_v[p - 1] < sa[n]) { ta_v[p]=ta_v[p-1]; ta_i[p]=ta_i[p-1]; --p; }
902	                    ta_v[p] = sa[n]; ta_i[p] = n;
903	                }
904	                if (sb[n] > tb_v[kb - 1]) {
905	                    int p = kb - 1;
906	                    while (p > 0 && tb_v[p - 1] < sb[n]) { tb_v[p]=tb_v[p-1]; tb_i[p]=tb_i[p-1]; --p; }
907	                    tb_v[p] = sb[n]; tb_i[p] = n;
908	                }
909	            }
910	            // softmax(top*T) per axis.
911	            float soft_a[K], soft_b[K];
912	            {
913	                float ma = ta_v[0], mb = tb_v[0];   // sorted descending → [0] is max
914	                float za = 0.0f, zb = 0.0f;
915	                // Accurate exp (expf, NOT ptx_expf): the reference PEER routing
916	                // (detail::peer_expert_forward) uses torch::softmax — accurate.
917	                // ptx_expf with the *T=10 amplification would diverge invisibly to
918	                // the fp64 mirror and only bite at the GPU parity gate.
919	                for (int i = 0; i < ka; ++i) { soft_a[i] = expf((ta_v[i]-ma)*T); za += soft_a[i]; }
920	                for (int i = 0; i < kb; ++i) { soft_b[i] = expf((tb_v[i]-mb)*T); zb += soft_b[i]; }
921	                for (int i = 0; i < ka; ++i) soft_a[i] /= za;
922	                for (int i = 0; i < kb; ++i) soft_b[i] /= zb;
923	            }
924	            // k×k Cartesian experts + routing-weighted MLP, accumulate.
925	            float head_out = 0.0f;
926	            for (int ia = 0; ia < ka; ++ia) {
927	                for (int ib = 0; ib < kb; ++ib) {
928	                    int eidx = ta_i[ia] * pkd + tb_i[ib];
929	                    if (eidx < 0) eidx = 0;
930	                    if (eidx > Dims::num_experts - 1) eidx = Dims::num_experts - 1;
931	                    const float rw = soft_a[ia] * soft_b[ib];
932	                    // expert MLP: ReLU(W1*g + b1) then W2·z + b2. W1/W2 are
933	                    // [num_experts, expert_hidden]; per-element scalar input g.

204	//  C2-GAP FIX (the whole point of this struct). Previously each mega_*.cu host
205	//  entry bound ONLY pointers + lr into FusedOptState and left every other scalar
206	//  at its struct default — which silently froze the math: bc1/bc2 == 1.0 (NO

208	//  == 1.0 (Prodigy d-adaptation inert), and beta1/beta2/eps/wd/alpha/lamb/
209	//  alpha_max/beta/neg_lr_scale/decay_factor never reaching apply_optimizer<>.
210	//  apply_optimizer<> already READS all of these from FusedOptState; the only gap
211	//  was that nobody SET them. This POD carries them across the host→kernel ABI so
212	//  the cell can populate FusedOptState with the live optimizer's real values.
213	//
214	//  Defaults here reproduce the OLD inert behavior EXACTLY (bc=gate=d_factor=1,
215	//  decay_factor=1, the same beta/eps/wd/alpha defaults), so a caller that does
216	//  not pass scalars yields byte-identical results to the pre-fix cells — the
217	//  widening is additive, not a behavior change for unset fields.
218	//
219	//  Per-tensor step count / bias correction (loud assumption): the megakernel
220	//  treats the whole flat param as ONE task, so a SINGLE (bc1, bc2) pair is bound
221	//  per call. That is correct ONLY when every parameter tensor shares the same
222	//  step counter — which holds in the grokking race (all params step together
223	//  every iteration). The host computes bc1 = 1 - beta1^step, bc2 = 1 - beta2^step
224	//  from that shared step and passes them here. If a future caller steps tensors
225	//  at different counts, it must call fused_step per-tensor with that tensor's bc.

229	    float beta1        = 0.9f;
230	    float beta2        = 0.999f;
231	    float eps          = 1e-8f;
232	    float wd           = 0.01f;
233	    float bc1          = 1.0f;   // 1 - beta1^step (un-inverted; apply divides)
234	    float bc2          = 1.0f;   // 1 - beta2^step (un-inverted; apply divides)
235	    float alpha        = 0.98f;  // meta-net strength / grokfast_alpha / neuralgrok alpha
236	    float beta         = 0.0f;   // neuralgrok beta (affine psi term)
237	    float lamb         = 2.0f;   // grokfast/grokadamw amplification (grokfast_lamb)
238	    float alpha_max    = 1.0f;   // SG15 per-coord alpha clip ceiling
239	    float gate         = 1.0f;   // SG11 cosine gate / SG15 sigmoid(accuracy) gate
240	    float d_factor     = 1.0f;   // Prodigy adaptive d (effective LR scale)
241	    float neg_lr_scale = 0.0f;   // Muon: -lr * ns_scale (2D NS-orth apply)
242	    float decay_factor = 1.0f;   // Muon: 1 - lr*wd (decoupled decay multiplier)
243	    // ── GrokAdamW append-only widening (decoder L3-TC conversion). Both default
244	    //    to the INERT value (0.0 ⇒ disabled), so every other cell is byte-identical
245	    //    (additive ABI, same contract as the original C2-gap widening above).
246	    float gamma     = 0.0f;   // GrokAdamW layer-wise β1 decay rate: β1_i=β1*(1-γ)^i
247	    float grad_clip = 0.0f;   // GrokAdamW global grad-norm clip (<=0 ⇒ no clip)
248	    // ── Prodigy append-only widening (decoder L3-TC conversion, STAGED global-d).
249	    //    The estimator scalars; defaults are eager/inert so every other cell is
250	    //    byte-identical. d0 seeds d_prev at step 1; beta3=sqrt(β2) decays the
251	    //    persisted (r_ema,s_ema); d_coef scales the candidate d (1 ⇒ no scale).
252	    float d0     = 1e-6f;     // Prodigy d0 (step-1 d_prev cold-start)
253	    float d_coef = 1.0f;      // Prodigy d_coef (candidate-d scale)
254	    float beta3  = 0.0f;      // Prodigy EMA decay = sqrt(beta2) (0 ⇒ no persistence)
255	    // ── Muon append-only widening (ViT L3-TC, STAGED NS). The eager Muon manages
256	    //    TWO param groups with INDEPENDENT hyperparameters: a 2D-matrix group
257	    //    (lr/momentum carried by the main lr/beta1 fields, consumed by the P2.7 NS
258	    //    + apply) and a 1D-weight AdamW group (muon.py:115-125: adamw_lr,
259	    //    adamw_betas, shared weight_decay). A single global scalar set cannot map
260	    //    the main lr/beta1 onto BOTH groups, so the 1D AdamW tail (P3) reads these
261	    //    aux_* fields instead. aux_bc1/bc2 are NOT carried — the muon branch

266	    float aux_beta1 = 0.9f;   // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[0] (eager adamw_betas[0])
267	    float aux_beta2 = 0.98f;  // Muon 1D-group AdamW betas[1] (eager adamw_betas[1])
268	    // ── LookSAM append-only widening (decoder/vit/mamba L3-TC, MODEL-COUPLED SAM
269	    //    2nd backward). rho = SAM perturbation radius; looksam_sam = the every-k
270	    //    SAM-step gate (1.0 ⇒ run the in-kernel perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g;
271	    //    0.0 ⇒ reuse the cached sam_dir, no 2nd pass). α rides the existing `alpha`
272	    //    field. Defaults are inert (rho=0 / looksam_sam=0), so every non-LookSAM
273	    //    caller is byte-identical (only OptId::LookSAM's model phase reads them).
274	    float rho         = 0.0f;
275	    float looksam_sam = 0.0f;
276	    // ── SuperGrok11/15 append-only widening (decoder/vit L3-TC, meta-net mu). The
277	    //    ONLY SG scalar that flows through here: the SharpnessMetaNet rescale (mu =
278	    //    rescale·phi(g, sharpness), supergrok11_sm90.cuh:130 / supergrok15_sm90.cuh:98).
279	    //    The phi WEIGHTS + sharpness are DEVICE pointers the cell binds directly (not

281	    //    st.rho); st.alpha carries the SG meta-net strength (the apply tail reads it).

283	    //    non-SG caller; layout stays byte-identical (only the SG P2.45 phase + tail read it).
284	    float sg_rescale  = 0.0f;

287	// Fold the runtime scalars into a FusedOptState (pointers are bound separately
288	// by each cell). Single seam so every cell applies the SAME scalar mapping — no
289	// per-cell drift in which field a scalar lands in. apply_optimizer<> reads these
290	// exact fields, so this is the bridge that un-freezes bc1/bc2/gate/d_factor/etc.
291	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ void apply_scalars(FusedOptState& st,
292	                                                        const FusedScalars& s) {
293	    st.lr           = s.lr;
294	    st.beta1        = s.beta1;
295	    st.beta2        = s.beta2;
296	    st.eps          = s.eps;
297	    st.wd           = s.wd;
298	    st.bc1          = s.bc1;
299	    st.bc2          = s.bc2;
300	    st.alpha        = s.alpha;
301	    st.beta         = s.beta;
302	    st.lamb         = s.lamb;
303	    st.alpha_max    = s.alpha_max;
304	    st.gate         = s.gate;
305	    st.d_factor     = s.d_factor;
306	    st.neg_lr_scale = s.neg_lr_scale;
307	    st.decay_factor = s.decay_factor;
308	    st.gamma        = s.gamma;       // GrokAdamW layer-wise β1 decay rate
309	    st.grad_clip    = s.grad_clip;   // GrokAdamW global grad-norm clip threshold

311	    // the reduced grad's global L2 norm and st.grad_clip, then applies it in P3.
312	    st.d0           = s.d0;          // Prodigy d0 (step-1 d_prev cold-start)

382	def _scalars(P, seed=0):
383	    # Per-tensor scalars mirroring the per-op layer-scaled betas/alphas. gru_decay
384	    # == beta1 (csa_hca_step_one: `gru_decay = beta1s[i]`). bc1/bc2 = 1-beta^t at
385	    # a fixed t so the single-step compare exercises bias correction.
386	    rng = np.random.default_rng(500 + seed)
387	    beta1 = (0.88 + 0.04 * rng.random(P)).tolist()
388	    alpha = (0.95 + 0.03 * rng.random(P)).tolist()
389	    beta2 = 0.999
390	    t = 5
391	    bc1 = [1.0 - b ** t for b in beta1]
392	    bc2 = [1.0 - beta2 ** t] * P
393	    return dict(alpha=alpha, gru_decay=list(beta1), lamb_eff=[2.0] * P,
394	                beta1=list(beta1), bc1=bc1, bc2=bc2,
395	                rescale=0.1, beta2=beta2, lr=1e-3, wd=0.01, eps=1e-8)

1607	                     gemm_impl="scalar",
1608	                     lr=None, betas=None, weight_decay=None, eps=None):
1609	    """Run ONE TRUE L3 fused TRAIN step (real fwd+bwd+opt) for an L3-REAL cell.
1610	
1611	    PHASE 1+2: for an L3-REAL cell ((transformer_decoder|vit|mamba3, adamw)) this
1612	    REPLACES the eager forward + backward + optimizer.step() with ONE persistent
1613	    megakernel that runs the REAL model forward+backward AND the AdamW update —
1614	    real model math, real optimizer math, ZERO intermediate kernel launches (the
1615	    owner rejected CUDA graphs; this is the chosen path). The caller MUST therefore
1616	    NOT run its own forward/backward/step for this cell; it uses the LOSS this
1617	    returns for logging.
1618	
1619	    The input path is carried through the existing ``ops.fused_step`` ABI (whose
1620	    pybind arity is pinned), packed PER MODEL into the single ``input`` tensor:
1621	      * int_tokens (decoder/mamba): ``input`` = int32 [B*(per+1)] = tokens[B*per]
1622	        ++ targets[B]  (per = seq: decoder 4, mamba 8).  ``tokens`` is [B, per].
1623	      * float_patches (vit): ``input`` = float32 [B*(per+1)] = patches[B*per] ++
1624	        targets BIT-REINTERPRETED into the trailing float slots (per = 16*49 = 784;
1625	        ``tokens`` here is the float patch tensor [B, 16, 49]). The targets are
1626	        carried via ``tensor.view(torch.int32)/view(torch.float32)`` bit-reinterpret
1627	        (NOT a value cast) so they are lossless for ALL int32 — dispatch.cpp reads
1628	        them back with reinterpret_cast<const int*>. This mirrors the decoder's
1629	        int pack: one contiguous ``input`` tensor.
1630	    ``params`` = the flat concat of ``named_parameters()`` (in order); ``state`` =
1631	    [m|v|extra] (3*total) + a trailing loss slot the kernel writes the mean
1632	    cross-entropy into. We read that slot back and return it.
1633	
1634	    State/params ownership (critical): the megakernel updates the FLAT param
1635	    buffer in place, so we keep BOTH the flat param buffer AND the [m|v|extra|loss]

1637	    reallocating per step would reset momentum and the run would never grok. After

73	
74	// mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc — the WIRED TC launcher. Boundary mirrors the scalar
75	// mega_decoder_real_adamw (dispatch.cpp extern-decls it with the same mirror
76	// types) EXCEPT it takes NO workspace pointer: the TC workspace is a different
77	// size from the scalar nCTA*total partials, so this TU allocates+owns it. `loss_out`
78	// still points into the caller's state[3*total] slot (dispatch reads it back).
79	//
80	// OPTID-GENERIC (owner baseline directive — all 33 cells on L3-TC): the fwd+bwd+
81	// grad-reduction is OPTIMIZER-INDEPENDENT (the same validated wgmma decoder kernel);
82	// ONLY the per-element optimizer TAIL (apply_optimizer<Opt>) differs, and that tail
83	// is the 14/0-apply-parity math already in opt_components.cuh. So this launcher
84	// takes `opt_id` (the OptId int) and dispatches to the matching kernel instantiation
85	// over the SAME state buffer. The state layout is [m | v | extra] (3*total) + loss:
86	//   * lion              uses m only (v/extra unread; bound harmlessly)
87	//   * adamw             uses m, v
88	//   * grokfast/grokadamw use m, v, ema  (ema == the `extra` slice, state + 2*total)
89	//   * neuralgrok        uses m, v, AND a psi-net weight pack the cell supplies in the
90	//                       `extra` slice (kPsiPackFloats floats); st.psi_W1/b1/W2 bind
91	//                       to those offsets, exactly as opt_components.cuh documents.
92	// The STAGED optimizers prodigy (P2.6 global-d) and muon (P2.7 grid-cooperative NS)
93	// ARE routed here: their precompute is an IN-KERNEL phase, so they remain a SINGLE
94	// persistent launch (the cases below). The SAM-coupled SG11/SG15/looksam and SG2 are
95	// NOT — they need a 2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd / a sharpness ABI field / a segmented sort
96	// that this single-launch path does not carry; dispatch.cpp gates them out (and
97	// wiring_check fails them loud with the cited reason). NeuralGrok is wired but its
98	// host-trained amplifier is a separate concern (the race fn gates it).
99	//
100	// ncta_cap: forwarded to the TC launcher (0 = one CTA/SM = full saturation, the
101	// shipped config). The race always passes 0.
102	cudaError_t mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc(
103	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params,
104	        const int* tokens, const int* targets, int B,
105	        float* state, float* grad, float* /*workspace_unused*/, float* loss_out,
106	        const int* sizes, const int* offsets,
107	        float lr, int step, const FusedScalars& scalars, cudaStream_t stream,
108	        int ncta_cap, int opt_id) {
109	    (void)sizes; (void)offsets;  // TC kernel reads kDecSizes/kDecOffsets directly.
110	
111	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
112	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
113	
114	    int dev = 0;
115	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
116	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
117	    int n_sms = 1;
118	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
119	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
120	    int nCTA = n_sms;
121	    if (ncta_cap > 0 && ncta_cap < nCTA) nCTA = ncta_cap;
122	
123	    const int64_t need = dec_tc_workspace_floats(T, B, nCTA);
124	    DecTcLauncherScratch& sc = dec_tc_launcher_scratch(dev, need);
125	
126	    // Re-point the ctx counters at THIS TU's cached counters (dispatch.cpp built
127	    // ctx pointing at its scalar DecoderScratch counters; the TC launcher zeroes
128	    // them per-launch, but they must be the ones this scratch owns so the grid
129	    // barrier is consistent with the workspace).
130	    ctx.g_next_task   = sc.g_next;
131	    ctx.g_arrived     = sc.g_arrived;
132	    ctx.g_generation  = sc.g_generation;
133	    ctx.n_tasks       = kDecNumTensors;  // parameter tensors for reduce+opt phases
134	
135	    // Bind the optimizer state slices. [m | v | extra] over the SAME state buffer;
136	    // each tail reads only its own buffers (opt_components.cuh guarantees unused
137	    // pointers are never dereferenced). ema/psi-net live in the `extra` slice.
138	    float* const m_slice     = state;
139	    float* const v_slice     = state + total;
140	    float* const extra_slice = state + 2 * total;
141	    FusedOptState st;
142	    st.exp_avg    = m_slice;
143	    st.exp_avg_sq = v_slice;
144	    st.ema        = extra_slice;          // grokfast/grokadamw slow-grad EMA
145	    // NeuralGrok psi-net pack (kPsiPackFloats floats at the head of `extra`): the
146	    // cell places [psi_W1 | psi_b1 | psi_W2 | psi_b2] there; bind the device pointers
147	    // so the apply reads real weights (psi_b2 is read on-device from psi_W2[kPsiHidden]).
148	    st.psi_W1     = extra_slice + kPsiW1Off;
149	    st.psi_b1     = extra_slice + kPsiB1Off;
150	    st.psi_W2     = extra_slice + kPsiW2Off;
151	    // PRODIGY (STAGED global-d) state bindings. The cell extends the state buffer
152	    // to [m | v | extra/s_track | loss | param_init | r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] (host
153	    // sizes it to >= 4*total + 4; see dispatch.fused_train_step). The `extra` slice
154	    // doubles as Prodigy's `s` trajectory accumulator (the apply reads st.s_track,
155	    // not st.ema — they alias here, harmless: Prodigy has no slow-grad EMA). The
156	    // trajectory anchor p0 (param_init) follows the loss slot; the 3 persisted
157	    // estimator scalars [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr] follow param_init. loss_out points at
158	    // state+3*total (dispatch's loss_slot), so param_init = loss_out + 1.
159	    st.s_track        = extra_slice;            // Prodigy `s` (per-element accumulator)
160	    st.param_init     = loss_out + 1;           // state + 3*total + 1
161	    st.prodigy_persist = loss_out + 1 + total;  // [r_ema | s_ema | d_lr]
162	    // LookSAM (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward): sam_dir is the PERSISTENT cached SAM
163	    // direction (g_sam − g), carried across steps in the `extra` slice (aliases the
164	    // grokfast EMA / Prodigy s_track slot — harmless: LookSAM has none of those). The
165	    // in-kernel P2.4 phase WRITES it on SAM steps; the apply tail READS it every step.
166	    st.sam_dir        = extra_slice;            // [total] cached SAM direction
167	    // SuperGrok11/15 (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu). State
168	    // layout: [m | v | mu | loss | sharpness(total) | phi_pack(4H+1)].
169	    //   * st.mu = the `extra` slice (recomputed each step by the P2.45 precompute; the
170	    //     apply reads it — it aliases sam_dir/ema/s_track, harmless: SG has none).
171	    //   * st.sharpness = loss_slot+1 (PERSISTED (g_sam−g)²; the P2.4 SAM 2nd backward
172	    //     writes it on SAM steps, the cached value is reused on intervening steps).
173	    //   * st.sg_phi_W1/b1/W2 = the phi pack at sharpness+total (host-scattered each step,
174	    //     like NeuralGrok's psi pack); sg_phi_b2 is read on-device from sg_phi_W2[H].
175	    st.mu             = extra_slice;            // [total] meta-net mu (P2.45-filled)
176	    {
177	        float* sharp_base = loss_out + 1;       // state + 3*total + 1
178	        float* phi_base   = sharp_base + total; // phi pack after sharpness
179	        st.sharpness = sharp_base;
180	        st.sg_phi_W1 = phi_base + kSgPhiW1Off;
181	        st.sg_phi_b1 = phi_base + kSgPhiB1Off;
182	        st.sg_phi_W2 = phi_base + kSgPhiW2Off;  // sg_phi_b2 read on-device from [H]
183	    }
184	    apply_scalars(st, scalars);   // FULL scalar set (un-frozen bc1/bc2/... + d0/d_coef/beta3 + rho/looksam_sam/sg_rescale)
185	    st.lr = lr;
186	
187	    DecoderTokenCtx tok;
188	    tok.tokens    = tokens;
189	    tok.targets   = targets;
190	    tok.B         = B;
191	    tok.workspace = sc.workspace;
192	    tok.loss_out  = loss_out;
193	
194	    // Dispatch to the matching kernel instantiation. The fwd+bwd is identical across
195	    // these OptIds; the template differs ONLY in the P3 apply_optimizer<Opt> tail.
196	    // Unsupported opt_ids return cudaErrorInvalidValue → dispatch.cpp throws LOUD (no
197	    // silent scalar/adamw fallback — the no-suppression rule). The STAGED/model-coupled
198	    // optimizers are intentionally NOT cases here (they cannot run as a single launch).
199	    switch (static_cast<OptId>(opt_id)) {
200	        case OptId::AdamW:
201	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::AdamW>(
202	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
203	        case OptId::Lion:
204	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Lion>(
205	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
206	        case OptId::Grokfast:
207	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Grokfast>(
208	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
209	        case OptId::GrokAdamW:
210	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::GrokAdamW>(
211	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
212	        case OptId::NeuralGrok:
213	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::NeuralGrok>(
214	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
215	        case OptId::Prodigy:
216	            // STAGED global-d: the SAME single persistent launch — the d-estimate
217	            // cross-tensor reduction is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.6, between B2 and P3),
218	            // not a separate launch. st carries param_init/prodigy_persist/d0/d_coef/
219	            // beta3; the kernel decays+accumulates the EMA, updates d, applies.
220	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Prodigy>(
221	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
222	        case OptId::Muon:
223	            // STAGED grid-cooperative Newton-Schulz (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME
224	            // single persistent launch — the NS orthogonalization of the 11 2D weights
225	            // (tok/pos/in_proj/out_proj/ff.0/ff.2/out) is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.7,
226	            // between B2/P2.6 and P3), grid-barrier-looped per matrix, NOT a separate
227	            // launch. The per-matrix NS scratch lives in the workspace (dec_tc_muon_floats,
228	            // carved after the Prodigy reduce slots). The persistent momentum buffer is
229	            // the m-slice (st.exp_avg); the 1D/non-2D weights take the AdamW tail in P3
230	            // reading the INDEPENDENT aux_lr/aux_betas (eager Muon adamw_* group). The
231	            // vit twin (mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu) proved this routing.
232	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::Muon>(
233	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
234	        case OptId::LookSAM:
235	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward (wave-2 decoder lane): the SAME single
236	            // persistent launch — the perturb→2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g is
237	            // an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.4, between B2 and P2.5/P3), gated to every-k SAM
238	            // steps by st.looksam_sam. The transient backup + g_sam buffers live in the
239	            // workspace (dec_tc_looksam_floats, carved after the Muon scratch); sam_dir
240	            // persists in the extra slice (st.sam_dir, bound above). The apply tail (P3)
241	            // blends g_adj=(1−α)g+α·sam_dir and runs AdamW. NOT a separate launch.
242	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::LookSAM>(
243	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
244	        case OptId::SuperGrok11:
245	            // MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward + per-tensor meta-net mu/gate (wave-3
246	            // decoder lane): the SAME single persistent launch. The SAM 2nd backward
247	            // (P2.4, sharpness=(g_sam−g)²) + the per-tensor mu precompute (P2.45,
248	            // mu=rescale·phi(g,sharpness)) + the per-tensor cosine gate are ALL
249	            // in-kernel phases between B2 and P3; the apply tail (sg11_sweep_b_step:
250	            // smart_grad=g+(1−gate)·alpha·mu, AdamW) runs in P3. The SAM scratch reuses
251	            // the looksam buffers (dec_tc_looksam_floats); sharpness + the phi pack ride
252	            // the extended state buffer (bound above). NOT a separate launch.
253	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok11>(
254	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
255	        case OptId::SuperGrok15:
256	            // Same SAM 2nd backward + mu precompute as SG11, but SIMPLER tail: the gate
257	            // is a host scalar (st.gate = sigmoid(accuracy)), NO per-tensor cosine stage;
258	            // the apply tail (sg15_sweep_b_step) does the per-coord alpha clip + smart_grad
259	            // = g + gate·a·mu + AdamW. Single persistent launch.
260	            return launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<OptId::SuperGrok15>(
261	                ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st, stream, nCTA);
262	        default:
263	            return cudaErrorInvalidValue;  // STAGED/coupled opt not single-launch TC
264	    }
265	}
266	
267	}}}  // namespace sg::fused::sm90

content.text: Now I understand the launcher boundary. The key constraint: the `mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc` boundary takes plain pointers + `FusedScalars` — NO header-only types cross. SG2 needs the full SG2Weights/SG2State/SG2Scalars bundle. This is the crux. Let me look at the SG2 standalone tail (sg2_meta_tail.cu) which already binds these, and the dispatch.cpp wgmma_tail_opt_id, plus the SuperGrok2 optimizer.

1	// csrc/fused/sm_90/sg2_meta_tail.cu — host-launcher TU for the SuperGrok2 FULL
2	// CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net persistent megakernel (csrc/fused/sm_90/
3	// opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh). This is the INTEGRATION seam specified in
4	// INTEGRATION-NOTES.md §1: the §1b host wrapper body lives HERE (a .cu TU that
5	// nvcc compiles, so the `kernel<<<...>>>` launch + the device-templated
6	// `launch_sg2_meta_optimizer_tail<Dims,...>` are legal), while bindings.cpp
7	// (host-only .cpp) extern-declares + PYBIND11-registers the two entry points
8	// (it cannot #include the .cuh: host gcc cannot parse the launch syntax).
9	//
10	// TWO non-template host entry points, both with a plain torch::Tensor / scalar
11	// boundary (the same boundary every existing SG2 launcher uses):
12	//   sg::sg2_meta_optimizer_tail(...)  — marshals the packed buffers + meta
13	//       bundle + scalars into SG2Weights/SG2State/SG2Scalars/PersistentContext
14	//       and launches the persistent megakernel (the launch-elimination of
15	//       csa_hca_step_one's ~15-20 per-tensor launches).
16	//   sg::sg2_ws_stride(int64_t Nmax) -> int64_t  — exposes the AUTHORITATIVE
17	//       per-CTA workspace stride sg::fused::sm90::sg2_ws_stride<SG2Dims<>>(Nmax)
18	//       so the Python driver's host stride can never drift from the kernel's
19	//       carve (INTEGRATION-NOTES.md §2 "Strongly prefer binding ... directly").
20	//
21	// SETUP.PY: this TU is globbed into _ops by `csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu` and owns NO
22	// PYBIND11_MODULE — so it is NOT dropped by setup.py's content-based filter
23	// (which removes only standalone-JIT cell drivers that define their own module)
24	// and does NOT collide on PyInit__ops. No glob edit needed.
25	//
26	// PRECISION / PARITY: fp32 throughout (matches csa_hca_step_one's fp32 compute
27	// and the parity-validated apply). Bit-faithful to the per-op math up to fp32
28	// reduction-order round-off in the hand-written GRU/PEER dots (the documented
29	// 1e-5 parity hotspots — see the .cuh header). NOT bit-identity.

32	#include <cstdint>

35	#include <ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h>

40	namespace sg {
41	
42	// Compile-time dims = supergrok2.py constructor defaults + OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS
43	// ["supergrok2"] (d_model=8, num_heads=2, gru_hidden=4, num_experts=144, ...).
44	// The race uses these defaults; a config with different shapes would template-
45	// specialize the launcher (compile-time dims). Mirrored in the Python driver +

49	// ── sg2_ws_stride: the AUTHORITATIVE floats-per-CTA workspace stride. The

51	//    allocation and the kernel's sg2_carve_ws can never drift. ───────────────
